subtitle: Music, empire and the nine moods of a Deccan king

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a moonlit palace courtyard filled with musicians around a seated king
panels.action: Ibrahim Adil Shah II sits cross-legged on a carpet in a Bijapur courtyard, tanpura in hand, eyes half-closed in trance as turbaned courtiers and veiled dancers freeze mid-performance under carved arches.

dialogue.text: In Bijapur’s golden dusk, Sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II dared a strange thing: he built power not only with forts and steel, but with ragas, rasas and a book of songs called the Kitab-e-Nauras.

i18n.hi: बीजापुर की सुनहरी शाम में सुल्तान इब्राहिम आदिल शाह द्वितीय ने अनोखी जुर्रत की – न सिर्फ किले और तलवार, बल्कि राग, रस और गीतों की किताब किताब‑ए‑नौरस से राज बनाया।

panels.shot: medium close-up of a very young prince on a throne, seen slightly from above
panels.action: A boyish Ibrahim Adil Shah II, slender and solemn, sits on a high Deccan throne, feet barely reaching the footstool, while older regents loom in the dim hall behind him.

dialogue.text: He came to the throne in 1580 as a child, in a court already cracked by factions, with Shia and Sunni nobles whispering, Deccan and Afaqis jostling, and the wounds of Talikota still fresh in memory.

i18n.hi: १५८० में वह बच्चा‑सा था जब गद्दी मिली – दरबार गुटों से दरक चुका, शिया‑सुन्नी अमीरों की कानाफूसी, दक्खनी और अफ़ाक़ी की ठन‑ठन, और तालिकोट की जख्मी यादें अभी ताज़ा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bijapur cityscape from a rooftop at dawn
panels.action: Ibrahim stands on a rooftop balcony at dawn, older now, looking over Bijapur’s clustered domes, minarets, and temple spires as smoke rises from courtyards and distant drums faintly sound.

dialogue.text: Bijapur in his youth was a city of many tongues and gods: Persian poets and Deccani bards, Sufi khanqahs and old temples, mercenary bands and merchants from the seas.

i18n.hi: उसके बचपन का बीजापुर कई ज़बानों और देवताओं का शहर था – फ़ारसी शायर, दक्खनी कव्वाल, सूफी ख़ानकाहें, पुराने मंदिर, भाड़े के सिपाही और समंदर से आए सौदागर।

panels.shot: intimate interior medium shot around a lamp-lit music lesson
panels.action: Inside a lamplit chamber, Ibrahim in simple robes sits before an elderly musician, carefully plucking a tanpura string as notated palm-leaf and paper manuscripts lie scattered.

dialogue.text: While regents guarded borders and bargained offices, the young sultan bent over instruments and verses, learning ragas, talas, and the Sanskrit idea of rasa from masters who themselves crossed worlds.

i18n.hi: जब वज़ीर सरहदें संभालते और ओहदों पर सौदेबाज़ी करते, नन्हा सुल्तान साज़ और शेरों पर झुका रहता, उस्तादों से राग, ताल और संस्कृत का ‘रस’ सीखता, जो खुद दो जहान जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ibrahim’s face lit by candle as he writes
panels.action: Ibrahim sits at a low desk, candlelight on his intent face, reed pen poised above a fresh folio as he contemplates, a tanpura resting within arm’s reach.

dialogue.text: From this inward schooling grew a question rare for a king: could he weave all these streams—Persian, Dakhni, Arabic, Sanskrit—into one river of delight?

i18n.hi: इसी भीतर की तालीम से बादशाह के मन में नायाब सवाल उगा – क्या वह फ़ारसी, दक्खनी, अरबी, संस्कृत – इन सब धारा को जोड़कर एक ही सुहानी नदी बना सकता है?

panels.shot: wide court scene with mixed gathering of scholars and nobles
panels.action: In the audience hall, Ibrahim sits in state as Sunni jurists in turbans, Shia-leaning grandees, Sufi shaykhs, and Hindu scholars in dhotis and tilaks stand in ordered ranks, their faces wary and curious.

dialogue.text: As he came of age, he shifted the court more firmly toward Sunni practice, strengthening ties with orthodox jurists and Sunni allies, even as Shia-leaning elites and other factions guarded their influence.

i18n.hi: जवानी पर पहुँचकर उसने दरबार को ज़्यादा मज़बूती से सुन्नी रिवायत की तरफ मोड़ा, सख़्त आलिमों और सुन्नी हलीफों से नाता मज़बूत किया, जबकि शिया रुझान वालों और औरों ने अपनी पकड़ ढीली न पड़ने दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ibrahim addressing the court from the throne
panels.action: Ibrahim, now fully grown, leans forward on his throne, one hand lifted as if conducting, while the assembled courtiers listen, some approving, some frowning.

dialogue.speaker: ibrahim_adil_shah_ii
dialogue.text: In this court, the law will be firm—and the heart filled with sound.

i18n.hi: इस दरबार में क़ानून सख़्त होगा – और दिल सुरों से भरा।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot of musicians in an open court, with Ibrahim at center
panels.action: Under a baradari with carved stone columns, Ibrahim sits among a semi-circle of male and female musicians—veenas, drums, flutes—while dancers freeze mid-gesture in ornate Deccan costumes.

dialogue.text: In this tension of creed and office, he carved a different domain fully his own: a court of sound, where musicians from north and south, courtly and temple, shared space under his listening gaze.

i18n.hi: इसी मज़हबी और सियासी खींचातानी के बीच उसने अपना अलग इलाक़ा تراश लिया – सुरों का दरबार, जहाँ उत्तर‑दक्षिण, महल और मंदिर के फनकार उसके सुनते हुए चेहरों के सामने एक छत के नीचे जमे।

panels.shot: close-up of the opening folio of a manuscript held in Ibrahim’s hands
panels.action: Ibrahim’s hands gently open a freshly bound manuscript, intricate Deccan floral borders surrounding neat lines of Dakhni script as he begins to read silently.

dialogue.text: Out of these evenings grew his Kitab-e-Nauras, a Dakhni collection ordered by the nine rasas—love, laughter, fury, compassion, heroism, fear, disgust, wonder and peace—an old Sanskrit frame filled with new Deccan life.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं शामों से निकली उसकी किताब‑ए‑नौरस – दक्खनी गीत‑माला, जो नौ रसों के हिसाब से सजाई गई – शृنگार, हास्य, रौद्र, करुण, वीर, भय, बीभत्स, अद्भुत और शांत – पुरानी संस्कृत चौखट में नई दक्खनी जान।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ibrahim composing with musicians around, in an informal setting
panels.action: Sitting on a low carpet among musicians, Ibrahim speaks a line while a scribe beside him writes, a veena player testing notes in the background, the atmosphere both relaxed and intense.

dialogue.text: In its songs he praised Saraswati, the goddess of learning, alongside the Prophet and the Chishti saint Bande Nawaz, not as a passing gesture but as a woven, repeated way of seeing the world.

i18n.hi: इन गीतों में वह सरस्वती विद्या की देवी की, साथ ही नबी और चिश्ती सूफी बंदे नवाज़ की तारीफ़ करता है – यूँ नहीं जैसे गुज़रता सलाम, बल्कि दुनिया देखने का बुना‑बुना, बार‑बार दोहराया गया नज़रिया।

panels.shot: close-up on Ibrahim’s mouth and tanpura as he sings softly
panels.action: Ibrahim’s lips are parted in song as his fingers lightly stroke the tanpura strings, his eyes closed, the suggestion of emotion at the corner of his mouth.

dialogue.speaker: ibrahim_adil_shah_ii
dialogue.text: O Nauras, nine treasures of mood—may each heart find its own color.

i18n.hi: ऐ नौरस, नौ रंगों के ख़ज़ाने – हर दिल अपना रंग पा जाए।

panels.shot: architectural bird’s-eye over the imagined city of Nauraspur in construction
panels.action: From above, we see the foundations and rising structures of a new suburb—Nauraspur—taking shape outside Bijapur’s walls, with courtyards, halls and gardens laid out in harmonious grids.

dialogue.text: To house this vision he fostered Nauraspur, a quarter whose very name echoed his book, a place for music and festivity within the architecture of rule.

i18n.hi: इस ख़्वाब को ठिकाना देने को उसने नौरसपुर बसाया – मोहल्ला जिसका नाम ही किताब की गूंज, हुकूमत की इमारत के भीतर राग‑रंग के लिए अलग मुकाम।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ibrahim walking through a painting atelier
panels.action: Ibrahim strolls through a workshop where artists sit on the floor painting delicate miniatures—court scenes, saints, musicians—while assistants grind pigments; he pauses to study one with quiet interest.

dialogue.text: Alongside sound, he nurtured image and text—painters crafting Deccan miniatures, chroniclers recording his age, and architects reimagining stone under his patronage.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ़ सुर ही नहीं, उसने नक़्श और लेखन भी सँवारे – देकनी मिनिएचर रचते नक़्काश, उसकी सदी दर्ज करते मुन्शी, और उसके साये में पत्थर को नया रूप देते मिमार।

panels.shot: dim interior shot of Ibrahim and historian Ferishta bent over a manuscript (Ferishta only implied as another figure, not separate cast)
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Ibrahim leans over a low desk with a seated court historian, pointing toward a draft manuscript while shelves of books line the walls around them.

dialogue.text: It was at his court that Ferishta composed his Tarikh-i-Firishta, a history that would outlive them both and carry the memory of the Deccan sultanates into later centuries.

i18n.hi: इसी दरबार में फ़िरिश्ता ने अपनी तारीख‑ए‑फ़िरिश्ता लिखी – ऐसी दास्तान जो दोनों से आगे जिएगी और दक्खनी सल्तनतों की याद सदी‑सदी तक ढोएगी।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of the Ibrahim Rauza complex under construction
panels.action: Builders, artisans and supervisors move like frozen ants around the rising Ibrahim Rauza, its domes and minarets half-complete, carved panels being hoisted into place under a hot Deccan sun.

dialogue.text: On the city’s edge, masons raised the Ibrahim Rauza, the sultan’s own planned resting place, its balanced tomb and mosque joined by ornamental stone that spoke both of devotion and imperial self-image.

i18n.hi: शहर की हद पर पत्थर‑तराशों ने इब्राहिम रौज़ा खड़ा किया – सुल्तान की अपनी सोची हुई मंज़िल, जहाँ संतुलित मक़बरा और मस्जिद को नक़्क़ाशीदार पत्थर जोड़ता है, जो भक्ति भी कहता है और शाही सूरत भी।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from the courtyard of the completed Ibrahim Rauza
panels.action: From the courtyard, we look up past silhouetted visitors at the completed domes and minarets of the Ibrahim Rauza, intricate carvings catching the light as Ibrahim stands small but central in the foreground.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions and later records anchor this complex firmly in his reign, a stone echo to the musical and literary program he fostered within Bijapur’s walls.

i18n.hi: क़दीमी लिखतें और बाद की खबरें इस पूरे रौज़े को पक्के तौर पर उसके दौर से बांधती हैं – बीजापुर की दीवारों के भीतर पाले उसके सुर और किताब के प्रोग्राम का पत्थर‑सा जवाब।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ibrahim in a more formal court session with armed nobles present
panels.action: Ibrahim sits upright in full regalia on the throne, guarded by armored nobles, as a messenger kneels before him holding a sealed letter, and distant cannon are glimpsed through an arch.

dialogue.text: None of this softened the hard facts of rule: campaigns, fortresses to hold, rival sultanates and the Mughals to watch, court factions to balance in a kingdom bound by both patronage and law.

i18n.hi: इन सब के बावजूद हुक़ूमत की सख़्त हक़ीक़तें नरम न हुईं – मुहिमें, क़िले संभालने, हमसाया सल्तनतें और मोगलों पर नज़र, और एक ऐसे मुल्क में दरबारी गुटों का संतुलन जहाँ रहमत और क़ानून दोनों से रस्सी बंधी थी।

panels.shot: introspective close-up of Ibrahim older, lines on his face, holding the Kitab-e-Nauras
panels.action: An older Ibrahim sits in a quiet garden pavilion at dusk, lines of age at his eyes, gently turning the worn pages of his Kitab-e-Nauras manuscript resting on his lap.

dialogue.text: By the time his reign neared its end in 1627, Bijapur had become known not only for its cannons and domes, but as a place where a sultan wrote songs and praised many sources of wisdom at once.

i18n.hi: जब १६२७ के आस‑पास उसका दौर ढलान पर आया, तब तक बीजापुर सिर्फ़ तोपों और गुम्बदों के लिए नहीं, बल्कि इस शहर के लिए भी जाना जाता था जहाँ एक सुल्तान गीत लिखता था और एक साथ कई सरचश्मों की हिकमत को सलाम करता था।

panels.shot: wide contemporary-feeling shot of an empty hall in Ibrahim Rauza with light streaming in
panels.action: An empty hall of the Ibrahim Rauza stands silent, pale light pouring through arches onto the stone floor where faint shadows of long-vanished musicians and courtiers seem almost to linger.

dialogue.text: His Kitab-e-Nauras, his court and his Rauza remind us that even within sharp lines of creed and empire, a ruler once tried to make shared beauty speak across them—and left moods that still reverberate in stone and song.

i18n.hi: उसकी किताब‑ए‑नौरस, उसका दरबार और उसका रौज़ा आज भी बताते हैं कि मज़हब और सल्तनत की कड़ी लकीरों के भीतर भी एक शासक ने कभी साझा ख़ूबसूरती को ज़ुबान देने की कोशिश की – और ऐसे रस छोड़ गया जो अब भी पत्थर और सुरों में गूंजते हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Nine Rasas of the Sultan

subtitle_i18n.en: Music, empire and the nine moods of a Deccan king
subtitle_i18n.hi: संगीत, सल्तनत और दक्खनी बादशाह के नौ रंग
